name: og-heredity
title: Chemical Heredity and Selection
concept: Heredity of the protocell: whether an inherited chemical difference is transmitted, carries selectable information at a feasible cost, and produces a reproducible fitness difference — one concept studied at several fidelities as arms.
gate_reason: Gate D (reproduction & heredity), the heredity half. Consolidates the campaign's heredity line into one concept with explicit fidelity-labelled arms: competing inheritance modules (og-06), the information-per-cost frontier of six mechanisms (og-06-alt), and the sharpened selectable-heredity test (og-34) — each judged against its own no-inheritance / de-novo matched null with input fluxes held equal. Headline is bounded by the sharpest arm (og-34, canonical): compositional inheritance yields a reproducible selectable fitness difference (+0.949 vs a no-inheritance control), QUALIFIED (template copying tracked as og-34a). Guardrail: the metabolism is the sustained A1 carbon-fixing network, not autocatalytic (A2 refuted).
claim: Across fidelities, an inherited chemical difference in the protocell is transmitted and selectable. Competing modules show heredity need not presume a long RNA template and that compositional / hybrid inheritance escapes the Eigen length catastrophe (og-06, supported); the information-per-cost frontier resolves which mechanisms transmit heritable bits per joule, attachment conditional on budget (og-06-alt, supported); and a daughter-inherited compositional difference produces a reproducible, selectable fitness difference — parent-offspring correlation +0.949 vs a no-inheritance control, with the population shifting under selection (og-34, qualified, canonical). Consolidated headline: qualified, compositional inheritance; template copying is the og-34a follow-up. Every matched null and arm verdict kept.
question: Does the protocell transmit an inherited chemical difference that carries selectable information at a feasible cost and produces a reproducible fitness difference against a no-inheritance control — and at what fidelity (compositional vs template)?
hypothesis: Inherited compositional differences are transmitted and carry enough selectable variance to shift a population under selection, without presuming a high-fidelity RNA template; the benefit is real but bounded (compositional, not yet template-copying fidelity). No heredity is claimed where an arm fails to beat its no-inheritance / de-novo control.
experiment: Consolidate the heredity studies into one concept with explicit fidelity-labelled arms, each preserving its matched null, verdict, findings and run provenance; report the consolidated verdict bounded by the sharpest arm (og-34, qualified) without over-claiming past it.
result: Compositional inheritance is transmitted and selectable — a daughter-inherited difference yields a reproducible fitness difference (parent-offspring correlation +0.949 vs a no-inheritance control) and the population shifts under selection; QUALIFIED (compositional, not template; template copying = og-34a).

arms.concept_role: First heredity: competing inheritance modules (RNA-template / compositional / hybrid / non-heritable) graded head-to-head above an error threshold — heredity must earn its keep, and compositional/hybrid escape the Eigen length catastrophe.

Information-per-cost frontier: six inheritance mechanisms as classes under a closing information ledger — which transmit heritable bits per joule, that heredity need not presume RNA, and that attachment is conditional on budget.

Sharpened Gate D: a daughter-inherited chemical difference produces a REPRODUCIBLE, SELECTABLE fitness difference — parent-offspring correlation +0.949 vs a no-inheritance control; the population shifts under selection.

findings.statement: A high-fidelity heredity module (RNA-like, 30-mer, per-site fidelity 0.99 → whole-sequence Q=0.74) retains functional information (C/(C+E)=0.62) and achieves net-positive lineage fitness (0.38) after its replication cost, outscoring the non-heritable control whose function degrades away.
findings.explanation: Real libRoadRunner quasispecies ODE; above the Eigen error threshold correct templates outreplicate the mutational error tail (Eigen 1971).

findings.statement: Heredity modules rank by an evidence-based head-to-head — RNA-like (0.38) beats the cheaper, lower-fidelity peptide module (0.24), and both beat non-inheritance — while a module below the error threshold (per-site 0.90 × 30-mer, Q=0.04) suffers the error catastrophe (retention 0, fitness −0.10).
findings.explanation: Whole-sequence fidelity Q = per_site_fidelity^length sets the threshold; longer high-fidelity polymers retain more information but cost more to replicate.

findings.statement: An agent-based LINEAGE model (individuals inherit a chemical phenotype at fission into a real tree) reproduces the Eigen error threshold (the imposed Q=fidelity^length relation) as a functional-persistence boundary in (per-site fidelity × length) space — AND shows that heredity need not presume a long high-fidelity template — compositional (GARD) and template-focused hybrid heredity persist at functional-persistence ~0.88 (seed-robust — 0.878±0.005 across the 5 graded seeds, 8/8 in a wider sweep) INDEPENDENT of length, where a long low-fidelity template collapses; the non-heritable control loses the parent↔offspring correlation (realized heritability ~0.04–0.11 vs 0.92–0.99 for the heritable modules) and crashes to ~5 individuals.

evidence.observed: compositional persistence 0.878±0.005 across 5 graded seeds (heritability 0.92), hybrid ~0.88 (0.92) — length-independent; template needs Q=fidelity^length above threshold; non-heritable heritability ~0.04–0.11, collapses every seed

findings.explanation: Coarse-grained agent-based reproduction with explicit fidelity/cost/competition. Template inheritance ratchets (Eigen 1971, no back-mutation) so a long low-fidelity template loses information; compositional inheritance drifts by multinomial fission of an autocatalytic composition (GARD, Segré 2000) — length-independent, so it escapes the length catastrophe. The realized heritability (offspring↔parent φ slope) separates true inheritance from the non-heritable control.

findings.statement: With heredity attached, parent and offspring phenotypes share information in every class — rna_like 1.46 +/- 0.10 bit, mineral_state 2.24 +/- 0.14, network 0.53 +/- 0.06, hybrid 0.49 +/- 0.03, compositional 0.47 +/- 0.03, peptide 0.14 +/- 0.22 (6 seeds; MI net of the permutation null, phenotype resolution 0.05) with realised heritability 0.45-1.0 — while every unattached control, whose daughters re-form their heritable material de novo from the same pool at the same price, transmits 0.00 bit with heritability < 0.01. Four classes (rna_like, network, compositional, hybrid) pass the strict pre-registered rule (MI converged on every seed, >= 0.1 bit, >= 0.05 bit above control); peptide fails because at q_p = 0.7 its whole-copy fidelity 0.06 sits below the Eigen floor 1/sigma = 0.33 and its function is lost before the estimator can converge; mineral_state fails convergence on one seed (bootstrap SE 0.15 bit) because its function decays as layer-copy errors accumulate at the nominal budget.

evidence.observed: 4/6 classes pass; controls 0.00 bit in every class; rna_like 1.46 bit, h2 0.93

findings.explanation: The information is measured on the phenotype (the function the heritable state confers), binned at a 5 % resolution so variation selection cannot see is not counted, bias-corrected (Miller-Madow) and reported net of a 20-permutation null; the convergence check is a time-ordered prefix ladder plus a bootstrap SE. Artifact: artifacts/information_frontier.json (classes.*.attached / .control).

findings.statement: Bits per joule span 3.8 decades across the six classes: mineral_state 5.4e19 (0 quanta, 0.1 quanta-equivalent per growth unit), network 1.3e18 (1 amino acid + 1 quantum per molecule), compositional 4.3e17 (1 amphiphile, 0 quanta), rna_like 4.9e16 (30 nucleotides + 30 quanta per copy), hybrid 2.5e16, peptide 9.0e15. Per offspring, rna_like spends 3.0e-17 J and 150 precursor molecules for 1.46 bit; network 4.2e-19 J and 4 molecules for 0.53 bit. Among classes whose estimate converged on every seed the Pareto front of (bits up, energy down) is {network, rna_like}; mineral_state (2.24 bit at 4.1e-20 J) would dominate both axes if certified.

evidence.observed: span 3.8 decades in bits/J; Pareto {network, rna_like}; cheapest and richest = mineral_state (uncertified)

findings.explanation: Costs are integer molecule and quantum counts drawn from the shared budgets by every copy event and converted with the package's 30 kJ/mol quantum and precursor energy equivalents (hypothetical); the InformationLedgerProcess integrates them against births and audits the store exactly (residual <= 3.1e-14 on 252 runs). Artifact: artifacts/information_frontier.json (frontier, ledger).

findings.statement: og-06's "heredity need not presume RNA" survives as a class-substitution result, but only in one currency: among certified classes the best non-RNA class (network) carries 0.36x the RNA-like bits per offspring and 26x its bits per joule; compositional carries 0.32x and 9x. Templated heredity takes over from the organic attractor classes exactly where the Eigen floor admits it — rna_like at q >= 0.967 (Q = q^30 = 0.37 > 1/sigma = 0.33) carries 1.45 bit against their 0.5; at q <= 0.95 it is not attached and transmits nothing. The template never overtakes the mineral class within the swept range.

evidence.observed: nonrna bits/J fraction 26 (network); nonrna bits fraction 0.36; rna_like overtakes organic classes from q = 0.967

findings.explanation: og-06 graded persistence of function; this study grades transmitted bits against their price, so the two halves of og-06's claim separate: the template is the richest organic carrier, the attractors are the cheapest. Artifact: artifacts/information_frontier.json (gates.nonrna_bits_fraction, gates.nonrna_bits_per_joule_fraction, fidelity_transition).

findings.statement: With the HeredityAttachmentStep deciding, compositional, network and mineral heredity attach from 3 % of the nominal matched budget (every feed and the power scaled together), hybrid from 30 %, rna_like only at the full budget (precursor ratio 0.74 even then, latched at the first full tick) and peptide at none (fidelity ratio 0.17): mean attached-fraction span low-to-high budget 1.0 over the five attachable classes. The step's budget thresholds (10 copies per individual, energy margin 1) are hypothetical and swept; its fidelity floor is Eigen's Q >= 1/sigma. Two budget-driven reversals appear in the map: the mineral class's function collapses as the budget rises (more layers grown per generation means more copy errors: 0.93 at 3 % to 0.15 at 100 %) and the network class's information vanishes at 3x (every core saturates its niche, so there is no variation to transmit).
findings.explanation: FMP 2.5 attachment as a lineage-level flag: before it, daughters re-form heritable material de novo and pay for it; after it, copies are partitioned at fission. Artifact: artifacts/information_frontier.json (attachment_map).

findings.statement: The fidelity transition reproduces the error threshold at the agent level with exact stochastic dynamics: rna_like keeps function only from q = 0.967 (settled mean function 0.22; 0.55 at q = 0.99) and is refused and non-functional at q <= 0.95; peptide needs q_p >= 0.90 over 8 sites; the 8-site hybrid template attaches from q = 0.90; the mineral pattern from p_m <= 0.005 per bit per layer (function 0.10 there, 0.71 at 0.001). The attachment step's analytic floor and the simulated loss of function agree at every swept point.

evidence.observed: rna_like attaches from q = 0.967; peptide from 0.90; hybrid from 0.90; mineral from p_m = 0.005

findings.explanation: Each template's own copy rate rises with its function (the master sequence copies sigma-fold faster), daughters inherit a random half of the parent's molecules, and bulk growth carries the cell-level selection; the common sigmoid landscape makes a 1-2-error neighbour functional and the tail not. Artifact: artifacts/information_frontier.json (fidelity_transition).

findings.statement: The vg-data package inheritance_budgets carries 39 parameters: 1 measured (the R18 polymerase ribozyme's 96.7 % per-site fidelity), 6 inferred, 8 extrapolated and 24 hypothetical, none unsourced; the mineral class's defect-copy error — the number that makes it dominate the frontier — is hypothetical with no measured anchor, and the attachment thresholds are hypothetical and swept.

evidence.observed: audit counts measured 1 / calibrated 0 / inferred 6 / extrapolated 8 / hypothetical 24; unsourced []

findings.explanation: The honesty indicator; the frontier's headline ordering rests on the hypothetical precursor energy equivalents and the mineral copy error, which is why it is reported as a frontier under stated costs, not a ranking.

findings.statement: There IS selectable chemical heredity (not the vasas-2010 null). Across 8 seeds x 40 generations at equal feeds, an inherited network-composition difference yields a reproducible parent-offspring fitness correlation (mean +0.949) far above the matched no-inheritance control (-0.018; permutation p=0.0001). Fitness is grounded in the real study-32/33 coupling (composition -> membrane retention -> standing pool -> division rate), so the correlation reflects a genuine mechanistic fitness consequence. Guardrail: selection acts on the inherited composition of the sustained A1 carbon-fixing network, not autocatalysis.

The inheriting population shifts composition measurably under selection (mean shift +0.551 toward higher-retention / longer-chain composition) while the matched no-inheritance control drifts (-0.004; permutation p=0.0002). Selection acts because both heritable variation and a reproducible fitness difference are present - the vasas-2010 evolvability caveat was tested (declared heritable variance sigma=0.03, not tuned) and the population shifts rather than drifts.

Heredity is carried by inherited NETWORK COMPOSITION (Option B, compositional / GARD-style), with the vasas-2010 evolvability caveat TESTED, not assumed - compositional inheritance carried enough selectable variance here for selection to act. Template copying (Option A, og-34a) is the higher-fidelity follow-on that would re-test selectable heredity under a copying mechanism, especially where compositional inheritance might prove too low-variance in other regimes.
